newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar says going ahead with Mideast economic meet.
newsitem.headline: Qatar says going ahead with Mideast economic meet.

text.p: Qatar said on Wednesday it was going ahead with preparations for a controversial Arab-Israeli economic conference, regardless of pressure from other Arab states to cancel or postpone it.
"Our main concern at present is to make arrangements for the summit and we are going ahead with it" said Qatar's Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ahmad Abdullah al-Mahmood.
He was talking to reporters asking him about the Middle East/North Africa (MENA) conference which is due to be held in Doha in November.
Some Arab states, angry at Israel's policies towards the Palestinians and the building of a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, have been trying to prsuade Qatar to cancel the MENA summit.
But Qatar has so far shrugged off the pressure, saying it was a commitment it had made at the last MENA summit in Cairo.

The MENA forum, an offshoot of the landmark Arab-Israeli peace accord signed in Madrid in 1993, is designed to promote peace through economic cooperation. It was earlier held in Casablanca, Amman and Cairo. Israel attended all three summits.
Asked whether Israel would be inivited to attend, Mahmood said: "As of now, we are only occupied with making arrangements... Invitations will go out only a few weeks before the summit date".
But Mohammed Ismail al-Emadi, assistant general coordinator for the summit, present at the news conference, said: "All those countries which had attended the Cairo summit will be invited".

Qatar and the Gulf Arab state of Oman have forged ahead of other regional countries in establishing economic ties with Israel after the 1993 peace agreement. But they have stopped short of full diplomatic relations pending a comprehensive Arab-Israeli peace.
Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak said on Tuesday his country had not yet decided whether it would attend the MENA conference.
Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Abdullah said in remarks published on Monday the kingdom would not attend the Doha gathering and that Riyadh had advised Qatar to cancel it.
